title: Guided Notes

vocab.Sampling frame: The list of individuals a study can actually choose from. Anyone left off the frame can never be sampled, however good the method.
vocab.Simple random sample (SRS): Every individual --- and every possible group of $n$ individuals --- has an equal chance of being chosen. Number the frame and draw, skipping out-of-range and repeat values.
vocab.Stratified sample: Split the population into strata (alike inside, different between); take a separate random sample from every stratum, in proportion.
vocab.Systematic sample: From an ordered list, take every $k$th individual after a random start, where $k = N \div n$. Only the start is random.
vocab.Cluster sample: Draw a few whole groups (clusters) at random and collect data from everyone in them. Works only when each cluster is a small mix of the whole.

lines: Answers vary --- most of the room says yes (``it was random'') or it depends.
(Settled at the end of section 2: no --- both rooms are 9th grade; not one senior was asked.)
A stratum: each building holds one unit type, so it is alike inside, not a mix.
Drawing three whole strata left every one- and two-bedroom household --- the car owners --- out.
Stratified, because the groups (unit types) are alike inside and differ on cars;
sampling every stratum in proportion guarantees the two-bedroom households are heard.
Only cluster --- it needs a list of groups. SRS, stratified, and systematic need every household numbered.
